summary: Tested venue guest ratings, host feedback and referral rewards. Backend: a new suite (test_nocturne_iter16.py) passed 12/12. The full regression ran serially (-n 0) in 3 foreground chunks and passed 219/219. Ratings: GET /api/venues and /api/venues/{id} return guest_rating (average, 1 decimal; 5+4+4 gives 4.3) and guest_rating_count. The count goes up with each POST /api/feedback, feedback docs store venue_id, and venues with no feedback return null/0 while the seeded rating is still returned. Host feedback: venue@ sees only feedback for venues it owns (none from Velvet Sky); guests appear by first name only with no user_id or email; admin sees all; guest gets 403 and no auth gets 401. Referral: an unknown invite_code returns 400 with a clear message. A blank code is ignored. Codes are case-insensitive. referred_by is set. The first paid booking via the credit path gives the referrer +200 and the friend +100, with ledger rows 'Invited <first>' and 'Welcome bonus · first night'. The card path via simulate_paid gives the same points, with nothing before payment and no repeat on a second simulate. A second booking gives no extra points, and a user with no referrer gets nothing. /me/invites counts are correct. UI (375x667): the sign-up form shows the 'Invite code (optional)' field and upper-cases it. A bad code shows the inline error 'That invite code doesn't exist'. Sign-up with 'ava1guest' set referred_by in the DB. The Profile invite-btn shows 'code AVA1GUEST · 1 joined, 0 pts earned' and Share sends the right message. The directory card shows '5.0 (1)' for Mirage and the seeded '4.6'/'4.5' fallback elsewhere. The venue page shows '5.0 · 1 guest rating'. The Host Studio host-feedback-card shows the average, stars, comment, first name and event. Also found and fixed leaks in older test cleanup (iter12/iter14), which were inflating the host Earnings figure.

minor.issue: reward_referral (and the booking email) runs inside the same try as fulfilment. If reward_referral raises after the ticket is issued, the except block marks the tx 'failed', sets needs_refund and refunds the credit, but the ticket still exists. Move the referral call outside the try or wrap it in its own try/except.
referral_code has no unique index (4 random hex chars + a name prefix). If two users share a code, find_one picks one of them at random. Consider a unique index or a retry when the code is generated.

One guest rating replaces the seeded rating completely (Mirage went from 4.6 to 5.0 from a single 5-star). The directory is still sorted by the seeded 'rating', not the shown value. Consider a minimum count (e.g. 3) or a blended average, and sort by the displayed rating.
No clawback if the first booking is later refunded or cancelled. Credit-only bookings (fully paid by reward credit) also count as 'paid'. This is a policy question; please confirm.

ui_bugs.issue: When navigator.share is missing (most desktop browsers and Firefox), Share.share rejects, .catch(() => {}) swallows the error, and the tap does nothing. Fall back to copying to the clipboard (expo-clipboard) and show 'Code copied'. Reference: /app/frontend/src/invite-row.tsx:14-17

issues: Google sign-in users have no way to enter an invite code (only the email form has signup-invite), so friends who sign up with Google can never be credited.

action_items: Move await reward_referral(...) out of the fulfilment try block in payments._complete, or give it its own try/except, so a referral error can't mark a fulfilled booking as failed or refunded.
InviteRow: add a clipboard fallback and a toast when Share is unavailable on web.
Optional: show the guest rating only after N ratings or blend it with the seeded rating, and sort the directory by the shown rating. Make referral_code unique.

Points $inc and the ledger inserts for the two users are not in a transaction (same pattern as feedback).
host_feedback limits items to 50 and the card shows 10. average and count use the full aggregate. Admin's filter {} includes every venue, as intended.

rca_of_issue: Host Earnings inflation: test_nocturne_iter12 and iter14 bought tickets via checkout (credit path / simulate_paid) and their cleanup deleted the tickets but not the venue_payables rows (record_id = ticket id), and did not decrement events.tickets_sold. Each regression run added +$120 for Obsidian / +1 Crimson Hour and +$160 for Mirage / +2 Velvet Sessions. Fixed in the test cleanup and verified with no change in payables count or tickets_sold after a rerun.
